battle.name: 丹瑞戰爭
battle.theater: 挪威東部邊境格洛馬河谷
battle.brief: 一八〇八年三月十四日，丹麥公使在斯德哥爾摩遞交宣戰書，瑞典腹背受敵：俄軍自東面進入芬蘭，丹挪聯軍則在格洛馬河谷與挪威東境反覆拉鋸。這支一五五〇年的西班牙火繩槍銃早已不是制式武器，但今日雙方火槍手營所用的滑膛燧發步槍，正是由它一脈相傳而來。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries:
交戰雙方是丹麥－挪威王國與瑞典王國，戰事在拿破崙戰爭的北歐外圍打開。丹麥－挪威方面的陸軍編制以挪威軍為主體：二十四個龍騎兵連約一千八百名騎兵、十四個火槍手營約八千四百人、十個射手連約一千二百人、十個後備營約五千人、八個擲彈兵營約四千八百人，另有六個要塞砲兵連約三百人、三個野戰砲兵連約三百人（其一、二號為騎乘行軍砲兵連）、兩個滑雪兵營約六百人、一個獵兵營約六百人（後增至七百二十人）、一個輕步兵營約六百人與一支工兵連約一百五十人。要塞守軍編制為：弗雷德里斯塔德要塞約二千三百五十人、弗雷德里克斯坦要塞約一千二百五十人、孔斯溫厄爾要塞約九百人、阿克什斯堡約八百人。挪威南方防線沿國境自斯維訥松德至特倫德勒姆編為約九千人，特倫德勒姆一線另約三千三百人，另有二千人駐特隆赫姆與克里斯蒂安桑、六千二百人駐弗雷德里克斯韋恩與卑爾根。丹麥本土軍雖可徵一萬四千六百五十人，真正能用來攻擊瑞典的只有約五千人。指揮系統上，挪威總督克里斯蒂安·奧古斯都親王同時主持挪威政府委員會；丹麥王儲腓特烈（後來的腓特烈六世）雖不情願，仍在拿破崙的壓力下同意宣戰，法國元帥伯納多特率法軍與西班牙、荷蘭部隊組成的聯軍屯駐丹麥境內，總兵力約八萬一千人。

瑞典方面，國境內可用兵力共約二萬三千人：南部七千人由托爾伯爵統率，指向挪威方向的一萬四千人由阿姆費爾特率領，諾蘭二千人由貝根斯特羅勒率領。西線大軍分左右兩翼，右翼由阿姆費爾特本人指揮，下轄加恩上校約六百五十人的飛行支隊、萊昂斯泰特上校第一旅約一千六百人、施維林上校第二旅約二千五百人、切德斯特倫上校第三旅約一千七百五十人、克龍斯泰特上校第四旅約一千七百人；左翼由韋格薩克少將率領，駐地分佈於斯特倫斯塔德、特夫特達爾與哥德堡至烏德瓦拉之間。編制主力是哈爾辛格、斯卡拉伯、卡爾馬、生衛兵與布胡斯蘭等步兵團，另配騎兵與隨軍砲兵。英國方面，約翰·穆爾率領的遠征隊於五月三日抵達斯堪的納維亞，至七月才改赴半島；五月十八日另有約一萬英軍抵達哥德堡，準備與瑞典聯手攻擊西蘭島。此外，一八〇八年三月至五月間丹麥－挪威海軍在波的尼亞灣與被海冰封住的瑞典分艦隊交手，並曾企圖在西蘭島方向登陸；法方的入侵計畫至四月中旬便被取消。
countriesEn:
The two belligerents were the kingdoms of Denmark-Norway and Sweden, and the war was fought on the northern periphery of the Napoleonic wars. On the Danish-Norwegian side the army was in substance the Norwegian army, organised into twenty-four dragoon companies of about 1,800 riders, fourteen musketeer battalions totalling about 8,400 men, ten sharpshooter companies of about 1,200, ten depot battalions of about 5,000 and eight grenadier battalions of about 4,800, together with six fortress batteries of about 300 men, three field batteries of about 300 (one and two of them mounted marching batteries), two ski battalions of about 600, one jager battalion of about 600 (later 720), a light battalion of about 600 and a pioneer company of about 150. The fortress garrisons were Fredrikstad with about 2,350 men, Fredriksten with about 1,250, Kongsvinger with about 900 and Akershus with about 800. The southern border line from Svinesund up to Trondelag was held by about 9,000 men, with a further 3,300 in Trondelag, 2,000 in Trondheim and Kristiansand and 6,200 in Frederiksvern and Bergen. The Danish army proper could muster 14,650 men, but only about 5,000 of them could be used for attacks on Sweden. The command structure ran through Prince Christian August of Augustenburg, governor-general of Norway and president of the Norwegian Government Commission, while Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark-Norway, the future Frederik VI, agreed to the war under Napoleon's pressure although he was reluctant. Marshal Bernadotte was sent to Denmark with a French coalition army of about 81,000 men in all - 12,500 French, 14,000 Spaniards, 6,000 Dutch, the 36,000 Dano-Norwegians and a Danish reserve of 12,500 - to prepare an invasion of Sweden.

On the Swedish side the forces available inside the kingdom totalled about 23,000 men: 7,000 in the south under Count Johan Christopher Toll, 14,000 facing Norway under Armfelt and 2,000 in Norrland under Johan Bergenstråhle. The western army was divided into a right wing commanded by Armfelt himself and a left wing under Major General Vegesack. The right wing held Gahn's Flying Corps of about 650 men in Dalby, Leyonstedt's first brigade of about 1,600 at Eda, Schwerig's second brigade of about 2,500 at Töcksmark, Cederström's third brigade of about 1,750 at Holmedal and Cronstedt's fourth brigade of about 1,700 east of Marker, while the left wing consisted of brigades posted at Strömstad, at Töftedal and between Gothenburg and Uddevalla. The infantry came from the Hälsinge, Skaraborg, Kalmar, Life Grenadier and Bohuslän regiments, with cavalry and foot artillery attached. On the British side Sir John Moore's expedition reached Scandinavia on 3 May and was transferred to the peninsula in July, and on 18 May some 10,000 British troops landed at Gothenburg in preparation for a combined attack on Zealand with the Swedes. In addition, between March and May 1808 the Dano-Norwegian navy fought a Swedish squadron in the Gulf of Bothnia and attempted landings towards Zealand, while the French invasion plan was abandoned in mid-April.
people:
北線最重要的人物是克里斯蒂安·奧古斯都親王。他是奧古斯滕堡家族出身，挪威海軍封鎖開始後被任命主持挪威政府委員會，戰時又兼任挪威總督，後來成為挪威事實上的統治者。他在斯馬連訥內的邊境戰役中採取內線作戰：把主力集中到受威脅的那一段，而不是平均分佈在一條漫長的邊界上，這一判斷在四月十七日、五月十七日與六月十日幾次戰鬥中都被證明有效。他麾下的旅長包括霍爾斯特上校（右翼旅，約三千四百人）、迪勒上校（中央旅，約一千九百人）、施塔費爾特上校（左翼旅，約一千三百人，戰後升任少將）、洛佐上校（第一預備旅）與奧默上校（第二預備旅），營級指揮官有駐弗雷德里克斯坦的尤爾中校、策劃六月南進的計劃者、以及普雷斯特貝克一役的希烏特費爾特上尉、奧勒耶方向的克雷夫廷少校與菲舍爾少校、在耶普塞特夜襲中率隊的耶爾根森上尉、在斯考斯貝格反攻中動用砲兵與四門臼砲的克雷夫廷少校。

丹麥方面：王儲腓特烈（後來的腓特烈六世）本不願與瑞典開戰，但拿破崙要求丹麥－挪威參加對瑞典的戰爭，他最終同意，並把目標訂在《布勒姆瑟布魯條約》與《羅斯基勒條約》割去的土地；法國元帥伯納多特被派往丹麥籌備入侵瑞典，他屯兵西蘭島卻久久不得進攻命令，其為人處事在丹麥與挪威民間頗得人望，後來在一八〇九年瑞典革命之後被推為王儲，一八一〇年正式當選，成為瑞典的攝政統帥。

瑞典方面：國王古斯塔夫四世·阿道夫在俄軍進攻芬蘭後本欲放手大舉入侵挪威，但英軍抵達哥德堡後改為籌劃英瑞聯合攻擊西蘭島；西線主將阿姆費爾特曾於一八〇七年率軍深入挪威卻無功而返，此次仍主張奇襲挪威，把失去芬蘭的損失用奪回挪威來補償。他手下的加恩上校以「飛行支隊」著稱，四月二十四日沿積雪道路深入而全軍覆沒；另有萊昂斯泰特、施維林、切德斯特倫、克龍斯泰特與韋格薩克等旅長，以及在北線擔任主力的托爾伯爵與諾蘭的貝根斯特羅勒。芬蘭戰線上瑞典有斯凱特與斯耶爾貝里等人；真正改變北歐命運的則是俄軍統帥巴克萊·德·托利，他於一八〇八年九月三日攻下芬蘭南部要塞，瑞典被迫北撤並走向與俄國的談判桌；卡爾·古斯塔夫·曼納海姆當年以少校身份在芬蘭軍中服役，據其傳記記載，一八〇八年十月在戰線上負傷被俄軍俘獲。戰後收拾殘局的則是卡爾·古斯塔夫·阿德勒貝里與尼爾斯·羅森克蘭茲，兩人於一八〇九年十二月十日在延雪平簽署和約。
peopleEn:
The central figure on the northern front was Prince Christian August of Augustenburg. A member of the house of Augustenburg, he was made president of the Norwegian Government Commission when the British blockade began and was also governor-general of Norway during the war, later becoming the de facto ruler of the country. In the border fighting of Smaalenene he worked on interior lines: he concentrated his main force on whichever section was actually threatened instead of spreading it evenly along a very long frontier, and that judgement proved right in the fighting of 17 April, 17 May and 10 June. His brigade commanders included Colonel Hans Gram Holst (right wing, about 3,400 men), Colonel Werner de Seues (centre, about 1,900), Colonel Bernhard Ditlef von Staffeldt (left wing, about 1,300, promoted major general after the war), Colonel Lowzow (first reserve brigade) and Colonel Ohme (second reserve brigade), together with company-grade officers such as Lieutenant Colonel Juel stationed at Fredriksten, the planner of the southern thrust in June, Captain Arild Huitfeldt who fought at Prestebakke, Major Krefting and Major Fischer in the direction of Ørje, Captain Jørgensen who led the night attack at Jerpset, and Major Krefting again at Skotsberg, where artillery and four mortars were brought to bear.

On the Danish side Crown Prince Frederik, the future Frederik VI, had no wish to fight Sweden, but Napoleon required Denmark-Norway to take part in a war against Sweden, so he finally agreed and set his sights on the territory lost in the Treaties of Bromsebro and Roskilde. Marshal Bernadotte was sent to Denmark to prepare an invasion of Sweden; he sat with his army on Zealand without receiving orders to advance, and the manner in which he behaved made him widely popular in Denmark and Norway. After the Swedish revolution of 1809 he was put forward as crown prince and was formally elected in 1810, becoming the regent and military leader of Sweden.

On the Swedish side King Gustav IV Adolf, with the Russians pressing into Finland, first wanted to throw everything into an invasion of Norway, but the arrival of the British at Gothenburg turned his plans towards a joint Swedish-British attack on Zealand. The commander on the western front, Armfelt, had already invaded Norway in 1807 without success and still pressed for a stroke to take Norway in compensation for the loss of Finland. Gahn, whose Flying Corps became famous, marched deep into Norwegian snow on 24 April and was annihilated; besides him there were brigade commanders Leyonstedt, Schwerig, Cederstrom, Cronstedt and Vegesack, with Toll and Bergenstråhle commanding in the south and in Norrland. In the Finnish theatre Sweden counted such men as Skytte and Sjöberg; the man who really changed the fate of the north was Barclay de Tolly, who took the southern Finnish fortress on 3 September 1808, forcing the Swedes north and towards negotiation with Russia. Carl Gustaf Mannerheim served as a major in the Finnish army and, according to his own biography, was wounded and taken prisoner by the Russians in October 1808. The men who closed the account afterwards were Carl Gustaf Adlerberg and Niels Rosenkrantz, who signed the peace at Jönköping on 10 December 1809.
kits:
卡面這件一五五〇年的西班牙火繩槍銃，在一八〇八年的戰場上並不直接出現——它是當日雙方真正使用的滑膛燧發步槍的直系祖先：同樣是一支單管長槍，同樣靠一點火星點燃火藥，同樣在滑膛裡打出一團破片，只是在一八〇八年，點火的機構已由火繩換成燧石，槍管旁多了一把刺刀。火繩槍銃本身的弱點在北境的天候裡格外明顯：它靠一根浸了硝石的繩索維持火種，一旦受潮或被雪水浸濕便整槍失效，而一八〇八年的挪威東境從二月到五月積雪未融、風雪不斷；射程短、不配刺刀，也使它在堡壘巷戰與夜間襲擊之外難以獨立作戰。

真正的制式裝備是滑膛火槍配刺刀：挪威軍十四個火槍手營共約八千四百人、十個射手連約一千二百人、八個擲彈兵營約四千八百人，都是以火槍為骨幹；投射武器另有龍騎兵二十四連約一千八百匹馬與兩個滑雪兵營約六百人，滑雪兵依賴雪橇、滑板與雪地行軍裝備穿過林線，構成北境冬春特有的機動力量。火砲方面有六個要塞砲兵連約三百人與三個野戰砲兵連約三百人，其中一、二號為可拆成馬車牽引的騎乘行軍砲；攻城只靠臼砲與小型攻城砲，攻城兵僅一百五十人，因此雙方對孔斯溫厄爾、弗雷德里克斯坦一類堡壘多採封鎖與包圍而少強攻。交通方面，挪威邊境多為泥路與雪路，軍隊依賴雪橇、馬匹、火砲馬車與人力馭運；軍需幾乎全靠海運，因英國封鎖海岸而屢屢斷糧；瑞典方面的交通線穿過大片無人森林與沼澤，一八〇八年三月的邊境遠征曾有士兵因雪崩與迷路失散。整體裝備水準可以從裝備年齡看出：挪威軍許多士兵的裝備已接近二十年舊，火繩槍銃一類更古老的火器只會殘存在徵發民兵與守備任務中；而真正決定邊境戰鬥勝負的，還是滑膛火槍的齊射、刺刀與野砲。
kitsEn:
The Spanish matchlock arquebus of 1550 on the card face never appeared on the field of battle in 1808; it is the direct ancestor of the flintlock smoothbore musket that both sides actually used: a single-barrelled long gun in both cases, fired in both cases by a spark igniting the charge, throwing a cloud of fragments down a smooth bore in both cases. By 1808 only the ignition had changed, from a match cord to a flint, and a bayonet had been added to the barrel. The weaknesses of the matchlock were particularly sharp in the northern climate: it depended on a cord soaked in saltpetre, and once that cord was damp or soaked with meltwater the whole weapon was dead, while in the eastern Norwegian borderland the snow lay unmelted from February to May and the wind never stopped. Short range and the absence of a bayonet meant it could rarely fight on its own except in fighting inside a fort or in night attacks.

The real standard equipment was the smoothbore musket with bayonet: the fourteen Norwegian musketeer battalions of about 8,400 men, the ten sharpshooter companies of about 1,200 and the eight grenadier battalions of about 4,800 were all built on the musket. For projecting force there were the twenty-four dragoon companies with about 1,800 horses and the two ski battalions of about 600 men, the latter depending on sledges, skis and winter marching gear to cross the forest lines, which was the characteristic form of movement in the northern theatre in winter and spring. On the artillery side there were six fortress batteries of about 300 men and three field batteries of about 300, one and two of them mounted marching guns that could be broken up and drawn by wagons. Siege work rested on mortars and light siege guns, and the pioneers numbered only about 150, so both sides generally blockaded and surrounded forts such as Kongsvinger and Fredriksten rather than storming them. In transport, the Norwegian border roads were roads of mud and snow, and the armies relied on sledges, horses, gun wagons and human draught; supplies came almost entirely by sea and were repeatedly cut off by the British blockade, while the Swedish lines of communication ran through great forests and marshes in which soldiers were lost to avalanches and to wandering astray in March 1808. The general standard of equipment can be read off the age of the gear: many Norwegian soldiers carried kit close to twenty years old, and weapons as archaic as the matchlock arquebus survived only in the hands of levied militia and in guard duties; and what really decided the border fighting was still the volley of the smoothbore musket, the bayonet and the field gun.
tactics:
這場戰爭的戰術可以分成三條線去看。

北線是典型的邊境小戰：兩軍沿一條數百公里的國境對峙，堡壘間距遠、兵力薄，任何一次襲擊都靠分遣小隊完成。挪威軍不求佔領瑞典土地，只求守住縱深幾公里的堡壘與交通線，因此大量使用哨所襲擾：五月十二日哈爾博·格倫上尉在斯特倫斯福斯以西連續襲擊瑞典前哨達半個月；五月二十三日耶爾根森上尉率輕步兵連與六十五名滑雪兵渡過格洛馬河，夜襲耶普塞特農莊，二十九名守軍中有二十五人被俘；六月九日尤爾中校策劃、由希烏特費爾特上尉率七百一十人南進，十日於普雷斯特貝克擊潰約四百二十名瑞典守軍，瑞典方面六十人死傷、三百九十五人被俘，另損失兩門砲，挪威軍的代價只有十餘人。瑞典則以縱隊與旅級支隊作短距離推進：四月十五日阿姆費爾特率一千六百人自埃達越境、沿利耶工事推進至格洛馬河；四月二十四日加恩上校以約五百人走積雪道路深入，企圖迂迴孔斯溫厄爾，結果在特蘭根遭挪威軍約八百人自側後攻擊，支隊被殲，四百四十人被俘，翌日在米特斯科根又有六十五人被俘。撤退與重整是另一端：五月十八日英軍抵達哥德堡後，國王命令阿姆費爾特轉入防禦，阿姆費爾特誤解命令，率第一、二旅退回國境，挪威軍得以推進至馬特蘭而未被追擊，瑞典入侵計畫遂告吹。

海線的戰術重點是破冰與封鎖：三月二十一日拉坦海峽一役，丹麥－挪威的分艦隊以破冰船隊衝入被海冰封住的瑞典分艦隊，雙方在冰縫中短兵相接；英國皇家海軍則以北歐海岸封鎖代替正面進攻，使丹麥－挪威的糧食、衣物與火藥無法靠海運補充，戰局往往不是被打垮的，而是被餓垮的。

東線是芬蘭戰場：俄軍自東面向芬蘭南部推進，瑞典守軍節節後撤，瑞典本土的兵源與物資須同時供應芬蘭與挪威兩條戰線，這才是這場戰爭真正吃緊的地方。多數與芬蘭相關的細節因雙方檔案散佚而記載有限，所能確定的是，瑞典最終在一八〇九年把整個芬蘭交給了俄國，而丹麥－挪威在芬蘭方向的小股遠征則隨之瓦解。
tacticsEn:
The tactics of this war fall into three separate lines.

The northern front was a classic border war: two armies held a frontier several hundred kilometres long, the fortresses stood far apart and the troops were thin, so every attack was carried out by detached small parties. The Norwegian army did not aim at taking Swedish soil; it wanted to keep the fortresses and the lines of communication a few kilometres deep in Norwegian hands, and it therefore leaned heavily on raids against outposts. On 12 May Captain Hans Harboe Gron made a series of attacks against Swedish pickets west of Strømsfoss that lasted half a month; on 23 May Captain Jørgensen crossed the Glomma with a light company and sixty-five skiers and fell on the farm at Jerpset at night, taking twenty-five of the twenty-nine Swedish defenders prisoner; on 9 June a plan worked out by Lieutenant Colonel Juel was carried out by Captain Huitfeldt with 710 men moving south, and on the 10th they routed about 420 Swedishmen at Prestebakke, the Swedes losing sixty dead or severely wounded, 395 prisoners and two guns against a dozen Norwegian casualties. The Swedes in turn advanced in columns and brigade detachments over short distances: on 15 April Armfelt crossed from Eda with about 1,600 men and pushed along the Lier entrenchments to the Glomma; on 24 April Colonel Gahn took about five hundred men along a snow-covered road in a bid to turn Kongsvinger, and was struck from the rear at Trangen by about eight hundred Norwegians, the detachment being annihilated with 440 men taken prisoner, followed by another 65 captured at Midtskogen the next day. Withdrawal and reorganisation formed the other end of the business: after the British reached Gothenburg on 18 May the king ordered Armfelt to take up a defensive position, Armfelt read the order as a general retreat, and with his first and second brigades fell back across the border, the Norwegian advance reaching Matrand unopposed and the Swedish invasion plan collapsing.

On the sea the tactical point was ice-breaking and blockade: at the battle of Ratan on 21 March the Dano-Norwegian squadron drove its icebreakers into a Swedish squadron frozen in, the two sides fighting at close quarters in the cracks of the ice; the British Royal Navy substituted a blockade of the northern coast for a direct attack, so that grain, clothing and powder could no longer reach Denmark-Norway by sea, and the war was often not beaten but starved.

The eastern line was the Finnish theatre: the Russians advanced into southern Finland from the east while the Swedish defenders fell back step by step, and the man power and supplies of the Swedish homeland had to serve the Finnish and the Norwegian fronts at once, which is where the strain of the war really bit. Much of the detail of the Finnish campaign is lost with the scattered archives of both sides, and what can be established is that Sweden ended up handing the whole of Finland to Russia in 1809, while the small Danish-Norwegian expedition in that direction fell apart with it.
data:
可核對的數字大致如下。一八〇八年三月十四日，丹麥駐斯德哥爾摩公使向瑞典政府遞交宣戰書。瑞典境內可用兵力約二萬三千人，其中南部七千、對挪威方向一萬四千、諾蘭二千。丹麥－挪威聯軍合計三萬六千人，其中丹麥本土軍可徵一萬四千六百五十人，但能用於攻擊瑞典者僅約五千。挪威南方防線約九千人，特倫德勒姆約三千三百人，特隆赫姆與克里斯蒂安桑二千人，弗雷德里克斯韋恩與卑爾根六千二百人。要塞守軍：弗雷德里斯塔德約二千三百五十、弗雷德里克斯坦約一千二百五十、孔斯溫厄爾約九百、阿克什斯堡約八百。挪威兵種細目：龍騎兵二十四連約一千八百騎兵，火槍手營十四營約八千四百人，射手連十連約一千二百，後備營十營約五千，擲彈兵營八營約四千八百，要塞砲兵連六連約三百，野戰砲兵連三連約三百，滑雪兵營兩營約六百，獵兵營一營約六百（後七百二十），輕步兵營一營約六百，工兵連約一百五十。法國聯軍總兵力約八萬一千人，其中法軍一萬二千五百、西班牙一萬四千、荷蘭六千、丹挪三萬六千、丹麥後備一萬二千五百。

具體戰鬥的數字：一八〇八年四月一日貝根斯特羅勒率二千人自耶姆特蘭入挪威，同日另有一支二百三十五人的分隊越境；四月八日班布率五百五十八人越境追擊，奪回包括二十二門砲在內的掠獲物。四月十八日利耶之戰，瑞典一千人擊敗挪威八百至九百人。四月二十四日特蘭根之戰，瑞典支隊被殲，四百四十人被俘，翌日米特斯科根又有六十五人被俘。五月二日至三日韋格薩克率約二千人自三路推進至弗雷德里克哈爾德以東，止步於哈勒羅德、耶德德魯德、恩寧達倫與貝爾比教堂一線；五月五日阿雷馬克交火，瑞典死十人傷十六人，挪威傷十人；五月七日菲舍爾部再戰，挪威傷九人。六月十日普雷斯特貝克之戰，挪威以七百一十人對瑞典約四百二十人，瑞典死傷六十人、被俘三百九十五人（其中三十四人受傷）、損失兩門砲，挪威傷亡約十二人。五月十八日英軍一萬人抵達哥德堡。疾病造成的損失極重：南方挪威軍約一萬七千人，一八〇九年三月有八千七百人進入野戰醫院，其中一千二百人死亡；瑞典軍的病患率由九月百分之二十二升至十一月百分之二十五，十一月單月死亡四百零三人。七月二日至十日，挪威以克羅格少將率一千八百人再攻耶姆特蘭，七月二十四日在赫耶達倫對上德貝爾恩上校所部九百人而敗，二十五日停戰，八月三日全部撤出瑞典。

芬蘭與波美拉尼亞一線：一八〇八年九月三日腓特里克斯哈姆失守；一八〇九年九月十七日瑞典與俄國簽訂腓特里克斯哈姆條約，割讓芬蘭、奧蘭群島與全部波美拉尼亞（含維斯馬）。當時芬蘭人口約八十萬上下，瑞典本土約三百五十萬。
dataEn:
The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. On 14 March 1808 the Danish minister in Stockholm presented the declaration of war to the Swedish government. Sweden had about 23,000 men available inside the kingdom: 7,000 in the south, 14,000 facing Norway and 2,000 in Norrland. The Dano-Norwegian army totalled 36,000 men, of whom the Danish army proper could muster 14,650, though only about 5,000 could be used for attacks on Sweden. The Norwegian southern defence line numbered about 9,000 men, Trondelag about 3,300, Trondheim and Kristiansand 2,000 and Frederiksvern and Bergen 6,200. Fortress garrisons: Fredrikstad about 2,350, Fredriksten about 1,250, Kongsvinger about 900, Akershus about 800. The Norwegian order of battle: twenty-four dragoon companies of about 1,800 riders, fourteen musketeer battalions of about 8,400 men, ten sharpshooter companies of about 1,200, ten depot battalions of about 5,000, eight grenadier battalions of about 4,800, six fortress batteries of about 300, three field batteries of about 300, two ski battalions of about 600, one jager battalion of about 600 (later 720), a light battalion of about 600 and a pioneer company of about 150. The French coalition force came to about 81,000 men in all: 12,500 French, 14,000 Spaniards, 6,000 Dutch, 36,000 Dano-Norwegians and a Danish reserve of 12,500.

The figures of particular engagements: on 1 April 1808 Bergenstråhle entered Norway from Jämtland with 2,000 men, and the same day a detachment of 235 crossed the border; on 8 April Bang marched across with 558 men in pursuit and recovered the booty taken in the raids, including twenty-two guns. At the battle of Lier on 18 April 1,000 Swedes defeated 800 to 900 Norwegians. At Trangen on 24 April the Swedish detachment was annihilated and 440 men taken prisoner, with another 65 captured at Midtskogen the next day. On 2 and 3 May Vegesack advanced about 2,000 men in three columns to the east of Fredrikshald and was stopped on the line Hallerod, Gjeddeludd, Enningdalen and Berby church; at Aremark on 5 May the Swedes lost ten dead and sixteen wounded against ten Norwegian wounded; on 7 May Fischer fought again and Norway lost nine men. At Prestebakke on 10 June Norway brought 710 men against about 420 Swedes, the Swedes losing sixty dead or wounded, 395 prisoners (of whom thirty-four were wounded) and two guns, against about twelve Norwegian casualties. On 18 May 10,000 British troops reached Gothenburg. Disease was ruinous: the southern Norwegian army of about 17,000 men saw 8,700 admitted to field hospitals in March 1809, of whom 1,200 died; Swedish sickness rates rose from twenty-two per cent in September to twenty-five per cent in November, with 403 Swedish soldiers dying in that month alone. On 2 and 10 July the Norwegians invaded Jamtland again under Major General von Krogh with 1,800 men, and on 24 July in Härjedalen they met 900 men under Colonel von Döbeln and were defeated; an armistice was signed on the 25th and the Norwegian troops were all out of Sweden by 3 August.

On the Finnish and Pomeranian side: Fredrikshamn fell on 3 September 1808, and on 17 September 1809 Sweden concluded the Treaty of Fredrikshamn with Russia, ceding Finland, the Åland islands and all of Swedish Pomerania with Wismar. The population of Finland at the time was on the order of eight hundred thousand, and Sweden proper around three and a half million.
cause:
這場戰爭的直接起因，是拿破崙的體系把兩個本來想保持中立的北歐國家推上戰場。一八〇五年瑞典加入反法同盟，同年拿破崙在西北德國推進迅速，呂貝克一役之後瑞典軍退守波美拉尼亞；一八〇七年法軍佔領瑞典波美拉尼亞，拿破崙提出以北歐的挪威交換波美拉尼亞，未被接受。提爾西特和約之後，拿破崙要把中立的丹麥－挪威拉入大陸封鎖體系，英國則害怕丹麥艦隊落入法國手中，遂在一八〇七年炮擊並佔領哥本哈根，俘走大部分丹麥海軍。丹麥－挪威隨即在楓丹白露與法國結盟，協議中法國含糊承諾協助重建丹麥艦隊，丹麥則須參加對瑞典的戰爭；一八〇八年三月十四日，丹麥公使向瑞典政府遞交宣戰書，目標是收回《布勒姆瑟布魯條約》與《羅斯基勒條約》割去的土地。瑞典同時面對兩個方向：一八〇八年二月俄軍越過芬蘭邊境，瑞典被迫把主力東調，阿姆費爾特遂主張趁機反攻挪威，把失去芬蘭的損失用奪回挪威來補償。

第二層原因在挪威內部。挪威在一八〇七年英國封鎖之後召開制憲議會，會中要求對瑞典開戰，並主張以戰功換取耶姆特蘭、赫耶達倫與瓦朗厄爾一帶的瑞典土地作為補償；由於挪威海岸線極長，軍隊大量投入海岸防衛，邊境部隊裝備陳舊、彈藥與衣物不足，許多士兵的裝備已接近二十年舊，軍中普遍認為出兵既是雪中送炭，也是為家園與邊地爭地盤。

第三層是邊疆的日常暴力。兩國邊界以山脈分水嶺劃定，定界留下的測量爭議從未解決，牧場、獵場與冬季牧養的界線年年糾紛；一八〇八年的挪威軍人不得對瑞典境內平民掠奪、掠獲須繳回，恰恰說明邊境摩擦已逼近失控，而四月初布雷肯一帶的相互掠奪與隨後奪回二十二門砲的報復行動，成為整條邊境線互相報復的開端。
causeEn:
The direct cause of the war was that Napoleon's system pushed two North European states that had wanted to stay neutral onto the battlefield. Sweden joined the coalition in 1805, and after Napoleon's rapid advance in north-west Germany and the defeat at Lubeck the Swedish army had withdrawn into Swedish Pomerania; in 1807 the French occupied that province, and Napoleon offered Norway in exchange for it, an offer that was refused. After the Treaties of Tilsit Napoleon moved to pull neutral Denmark-Norway into the Continental System, while Britain, fearing that the Danish fleet would fall to France, bombarded and occupied Copenhagen in 1807 and captured most of the Danish navy. Denmark-Norway then allied itself with France at Fontainebleau, the agreement giving only vague French promises to help rebuild the Danish fleet while Denmark undertook to join a war against Sweden; on 14 March 1808 the Danish minister in Stockholm presented the declaration of war to the Swedish government, with the aim of recovering the territory lost in the Treaties of Bromsebro and Roskilde. Sweden was squeezed at the same time from two sides: Russian troops crossed the Finnish frontier in February 1808, Sweden had to move its strength eastward, and Armfelt accordingly argued for a counter-stroke into Norway so that the loss of Finland might be made good by the taking of Norway.

The second layer of cause lay inside Norway. After the British blockade of 1807 a constituent assembly met in Norway, demanding war against Sweden and claiming Swedish lands around Jamtland, Härjedalen and Varanger in recompense for the fighting. Because the Norwegian coastline is so long, the army was heavily committed to coastal defence, the border troops were poorly supplied with weapons, ammunition and clothing, and much of their equipment was close to twenty years old; the army at large held that going to war was both a duty to a friendly state and a way to win land for the homeland.

The third layer was the ordinary violence of the frontier. The border between the two countries was drawn along the watershed, and the survey disputes left by the boundary commission were never settled, so the lines of pasture, hunting and winter feeding were disputed every year. The fact that Norwegian soldiers in 1808 were forbidden to plunder Swedish civilians and had to hand back what they had taken shows how close the friction had come to running away, and the mutual raids around Brekken in early April, followed by the counter-stroke that recovered twenty-two guns, opened a round of reprisals along the whole frontier.
impact:
第一層影響是北歐王權的轉向。一八〇九年三月七日阿德勒斯帕雷在卡爾斯塔德舉起叛旗向斯德哥爾摩進軍，三月十三日阿德勒克魯茨等七名密謀者闖入王宮，把古斯塔夫四世拘禁於格里普斯堡，六月五日其叔父卡爾十三世即位，隔日制憲議會通過憲法，瑞典由專制王權轉入新王統治時期。值得注意的是，倒戈的北方軍隊在三月達成的孔斯溫厄爾默契中按兵不動，避免了北歐國家之間的內戰，因此一八〇九年並未出現挪威軍隊趁亂南下的局面。

第二層是丹麥－挪威的戰後處境：英國的海上封鎖切斷了它的糧食與軍需，遠征軍在異國作戰而本土卻為飢荒所困，執政的腓特烈六世最終在一八一三年被迫加入反法同盟，與英國結盟對付法國，而在一八一四年基爾條約中把挪威割給瑞典，換取英國的支持與英軍介入丹麥；帶頭促成這場交易的正是當年屯兵西蘭島的法國元帥伯納多特，此時已是瑞典攝政王與北歐的實際軍事主導者。挪威隨即以武裝起義反抗，最終在一八一四年底重新與瑞典合併時，協議維持了挪威的憲法與國會體制。

第三層在瑞典：這場戰爭與其說打垮了丹麥－挪威，不如說是把瑞典推向了與俄國的談判桌。一八〇九年九月十七日腓特里克斯哈姆條約簽訂，瑞典割讓芬蘭、奧蘭群島與全部波美拉尼亞（含維斯馬），約八十萬人口的芬蘭自此脫離瑞典，瑞典王國縮成只剩本土與南部屬地的小國；此後數十年，瑞典在本土完成常備軍與徵兵制的改革，國防財政為此重整，國王的臣民與議會之間的關係也因之重新排列。

第四層在軍事技術與戰術上：北境這場以小分隊襲擾堡壘前哨、滑雪兵穿越林線、砲兵只配野戰砲與臼砲的邊境戰，說明在沒有大軍展開空間的環境下，分散、小隊、燃料與糧食的爭奪比會戰更決定勝負；它同時也讓北歐的將領第一次在實戰中體會到，遠征的戰爭若沒有海運補給線，等於把戰爭綁在一條隨時可能被切斷的繩子上。
impactEn:
The first layer of impact was the change of direction in the northern monarchies. On 7 March 1809 Adlersparre raised the flag of rebellion at Karlstad and marched on Stockholm; on 13 March Adlercreutz and six other conspirators broke into the royal apartments and seized the king, who was shut up in Gripsholm; on 5 June his uncle Charles XIII was elected king, and a constitution was passed by an assembly of nobles, clergy, bourgeoisie and peasants the following day, so that Sweden moved from absolute monarchy into a new kind of royal government. It is worth noting that the rebel northern army stood fast under the Kongsvinger agreement of March and did not march south, which avoided a civil war between the Nordic countries; no Norwegian army came over the border in 1809.

The second layer was the post-war condition of Denmark-Norway: the British maritime blockade cut its grain and military supplies, the expeditionary armies fought abroad while the homeland went hungry, and the reigning Frederik VI was finally forced in 1813 to join the anti-French coalition and ally with Britain against France; in the Treaty of Kiel of 1814 he ceded Norway to Sweden in exchange for British support and British intervention in Denmark. The man who drove that transaction was the very marshal who had once sat with his army on Zealand, Bernadotte, by then regent of Sweden and the real military leader of the north. Norway answered with an armed rising, and when the two were reunited at the end of 1814 the agreement preserved Norway's constitution and its parliament.

The third layer fell on Sweden: rather than beating Denmark-Norway, this war pushed Sweden to the negotiating table with Russia. By the Treaty of Fredrikshamn of 17 September 1809 Sweden ceded Finland, the Åland islands and all of Swedish Pomerania with Wismar, and a population of some eight hundred thousand in Finland left the Swedish realm, reducing the Swedish state to its homeland and a few southern dependencies. In the decades that followed the standing army and the conscription system were reformed at home, the defence finances were reorganised, and the relationship between the king, his subjects and the diet was reordered in the process.

The fourth layer was military technique and tactics: this border war of small detachments raiding fortified outposts, ski troops crossing the forest lines and an artillery of field guns and mortars alone showed that where there is no room to deploy massed armies, dispersal, small units, fuel and the struggle for food decide the outcome more than set-piece battle. It also taught the northern commanders, at first hand, that a war of expedition without a sea-borne supply line is a war tied to a rope that can be cut at any moment.
result:
一八〇九年十二月十日，丹麥－挪威與瑞典在延雪平簽訂和約，簽約者是丹麥的尼爾斯·羅森克蘭茲與瑞典的卡爾·古斯塔夫·阿德勒貝里。和約維持戰前狀態，兩國互不割地，瑞典承諾把英國皇家海軍的戰艦與瑞典海岸保持一定距離，並處理逃兵與罪犯的引渡。對這場戰爭的結果，史家至今有分歧：有人認為雙方都沒有達成目標，是一場不了了之；瑞典史家烏爾夫·松德貝里則主張這是瑞典的勝利，因為瑞典守住了本土與波美拉尼亞，又迫使丹麥－挪威放棄在北境的攻勢，而代價只是丟掉早已守不住的芬蘭。

芬蘭線上的結局並不在這份和約裡。一八〇八年九月三日，瑞典在芬蘭南部的要塞腓特里克斯哈姆被俄軍攻破，瑞典在芬蘭的野戰兵被迫北撤，捱過一整個沒有會戰的冬天之後，一八〇九年九月十七日瑞典與俄國在腓特里克斯哈姆簽約，割讓芬蘭、奧蘭群島與波美拉尼亞，瑞典在北歐的實力從此改寫。戰爭的最後一幕則在挪威境內：一八〇九年七月二日克里斯蒂安·奧古斯都下令再攻耶姆特蘭，十日由克羅格少將率一千八百人越境，十六日奪下希耶爾佩塹壕以及莫爾西爾與馬特馬爾；因傳聞瑞典已與俄國議和，進攻方向改為赫耶達倫，七月二十四日在貝爾克奧森一帶與德貝爾恩上校所部九百人交戰而敗，二十五日簽訂停戰協議，挪威軍於八月三日全部撤出瑞典。

除此以外，十二月的和約並沒有解決真正的問題：它把爭端推遲，而北歐三國在隨後數年裡各自捱過戰爭、物資短缺與政治變動；直到一八一四年基爾條約，挪威才真正離開丹麥－挪威，而且是在武裝起義之後，才以另一種形式回到瑞典的統治之下，並且是以承認自身憲法與國會作為代價。
resultEn:
On 10 December 1809 Denmark-Norway and Sweden concluded a peace at Jonkoping, the signatories being Niels Rosenkrantz for Denmark and Carl Gustaf Adlerberg for Sweden. The treaty restored the status quo ante bellum: neither side ceded territory, Sweden undertook to keep the Royal Navy's warships at a certain distance from its coast, and the extradition of renegades and criminals was arranged. The result of the war remains disputed among historians. Some hold that neither side achieved its object and that the war ended inconclusively; the Swedish historian Ulf Sundberg argues instead that it was a Swedish victory, since Sweden held its homeland and Pomerania, forced Denmark-Norway to abandon its offensive on the northern front, and paid only for a Finland it could no longer keep.

The outcome on the Finnish line does not lie in that treaty. On 3 September 1808 the Swedish fortress of Fredrikshamn in southern Finland was taken by the Russians, the Swedish field army in Finland was driven north, and after a whole winter without a pitched battle the Treaty of Fredrikshamn of 17 September 1809 handed Finland, the Åland islands and Pomerania over to Russia, rewriting Sweden's position in the north. The last episode of the war took place inside Norway: on 2 July 1809 Christian August ordered another attack on Jamtland, on the 10th Major General von Krogh took 1,800 men across the border, and on the 16th they seized the Hjarpe entrenchment together with Morsil and Mattmar; hearing a rumour that Sweden had begun peace talks with Russia, they turned their attack towards Härjedalen, and on 24 July they were defeated near Bleckasen by 900 men under Colonel von Döbeln. An armistice was signed on the 25th and the Norwegian troops were all out of Sweden by 3 August.

Apart from that, the December treaty settled nothing: it postponed the dispute, and the three Nordic countries each went through war, scarcity and political convulsion in the years that followed. Only with the Treaty of Kiel of 1814 did Norway really leave Denmark-Norway, and then only after an armed rising, and only by returning in a new form to Swedish rule at the price of having its constitution and its parliament recognised.
